*vidtv_s302m_encoder_init(struct vidtv_s302m_encoder_init_args args)
{
	u32 priv_sz = sizeof(struct vidtv_s302m_ctx);
	struct vidtv_s302m_ctx *ctx;
	struct vidtv_encoder *e;

	e = kzalloc(sizeof(*e), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!e)
		return NULL;

	e->id = S302M;

	if (args.name)
		e->name = kstrdup(args.name, GFP_KERNEL);

	e->encoder_buf = vzalloc(VIDTV_S302M_BUF_SZ);
	e->encoder_buf_sz = VIDTV_S302M_BUF_SZ;
	e->encoder_buf_offset = 0;

	e->sample_count = 0;

	e->src_buf = (args.src_buf) ? args.src_buf : NULL;
	e->src_buf_sz = (args.src_buf) ? args.src_buf_sz : 0;
	e->src_buf_offset = 0;

	e->is_video_encoder = false;

	ctx = kzalloc(priv_sz, GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!ctx) {
		kfree(e);
		return NULL;
	}

	e->ctx = ctx;
	ctx->last_duration = 0;

	e->encode = vidtv_s302m_encode;
	e->clear = vidtv_s302m_clear;

	e->es_pid = cpu_to_be16(args.es_pid);
	e->stream_id = cpu_to_be16(PES_PRIVATE_STREAM_1);

	e->sync = args.sync;
	e->sampling_rate_hz = S302M_SAMPLING_RATE_HZ;

	e->last_sample_cb = args.last_sample_cb;

	e->destroy = vidtv_s302m_encoder_destroy;

	if (args.head) {
		while (args.head->next)
			args.head = args.head->next;

		args.head->next = e;
	}

	e->next = NULL;

	return e;
}

lprn_is_black(gx_device_printer * pdev, int r, int h, int bx)
{
    gx_device_lprn *const lprn = (gx_device_lprn *) pdev;

    int bh = lprn->nBh;
    int bpl = gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line(pdev);
    int x, y, y0;
    byte *p;
    int maxY = lprn->BlockLine / lprn->nBh * lprn->nBh;

    y0 = (r + h - bh) % maxY;
    for (y = 0; y < bh; y++) {
        p = &lprn->ImageBuf[(y0 + y) * bpl + bx * lprn->nBw];
        for (x = 0; x < lprn->nBw; x++) {
            /* bpl isn't necessarily a multiple of lprn->nBw, so
            we need to explicitly stop after the last byte in this
            line to avoid accessing either the next line's data or
            going off the end of our buffer completely. This avoids
            https://bugs.ghostscript.com/show_bug.cgi?id=701785. */
            if (bx * lprn->nBw + x >= bpl)  break;
            if (p[x] != 0)
                return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

struct sctp_chunk *sctp_make_strreset_req(
					const struct sctp_association *asoc,
					__u16 stream_num, __be16 *stream_list,
					bool out, bool in)
{
	__u16 stream_len = stream_num * sizeof(__u16);
	struct sctp_strreset_outreq outreq;
	struct sctp_strreset_inreq inreq;
	struct sctp_chunk *retval;
	__u16 outlen, inlen;

	outlen = (sizeof(outreq) + stream_len) * out;
	inlen = (sizeof(inreq) + stream_len) * in;

	retval = sctp_make_reconf(asoc, outlen + inlen);
	if (!retval)
		return NULL;

	if (outlen) {
		outreq.param_hdr.type = SCTP_PARAM_RESET_OUT_REQUEST;
		outreq.param_hdr.length = htons(outlen);
		outreq.request_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_outseq);
		outreq.response_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_inseq - 1);
		outreq.send_reset_at_tsn = htonl(asoc->next_tsn - 1);

		sctp_addto_chunk(retval, sizeof(outreq), &outreq);

		if (stream_len)
			sctp_addto_chunk(retval, stream_len, stream_list);
	}

	if (inlen) {
		inreq.param_hdr.type = SCTP_PARAM_RESET_IN_REQUEST;
		inreq.param_hdr.length = htons(inlen);
		inreq.request_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_outseq + out);

		sctp_addto_chunk(retval, sizeof(inreq), &inreq);

		if (stream_len)
			sctp_addto_chunk(retval, stream_len, stream_list);
	}

	return retval;
}

static char ** split(const char *arg, const char *delim) {
  char *copy = dupstr(arg);
  char **result = NULL;
  int i = 0;

  for (char *cptr = strtok(copy, delim); cptr; cptr = strtok(NULL, delim)) {
    char **tmp = realloc (result, sizeof *result * (i + 1));
    if (!tmp && result) {
      while (i > 0) {
	free(result[--i]);
      }
      free(result);
      free(copy);
      return NULL;
    }
    result = tmp;
    result[i++] = dupstr(cptr);
  }

  free(copy);

  if (i) {
    char **tmp = realloc(result, sizeof *result * (i + 1));
    if (!tmp) {
      while (i > 0) {
	free(result[--i]);
      }
      free(result);
      return NULL;
    }
    result = tmp;
    result[i++] = NULL;
  }

  return result;
}

  - All resource lifecycle operations (alloc/free, open/close, lock/unlock, init/cleanup)

NUMERIC SAFETY:

- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.

static void build_dirs(char *src, char *dst, size_t src_prefix_len, size_t dst_prefix_len) {
	char *p = src + src_prefix_len + 1;
	char *q = dst + dst_prefix_len + 1;
	char *r = dst + dst_prefix_len;
	struct stat s;
	bool last = false;
	*r = '\0';
	for (; !last; p++, q++) {
		if (*p == '\0') {
			last = true;
		}
		if (*p == '\0' || (*p == '/' && *(p - 1) != '/')) {

static char ** split(const char *arg, const char *delim) {
  char *copy = dupstr(arg);
  char **result = NULL;
  int i = 0;

  for (char *cptr = strtok(copy, delim); cptr; cptr = strtok(NULL, delim)) {
    char **tmp = realloc (result, sizeof *result * (i + 1));
    if (!tmp && result) {
      while (i > 0) {
	free(result[--i]);
      }
      free(result);
      free(copy);
      return NULL;
    }
    result = tmp;

      }
      free(result);

    }

static void build_dirs(char *src, char *dst, size_t src_prefix_len, size_t dst_prefix_len) {
	char *p = src + src_prefix_len + 1;
	char *q = dst + dst_prefix_len + 1;
	char *r = dst + dst_prefix_len;
	struct stat s;
	bool last = false;
	*r = '\0';
	for (; !last; p++, q++) {
		if (*p == '\0') {
			last = true;
		}
		if (*p == '\0' || (*p == '/' && *(p - 1) != '/')) {
			// We found a new component of our src path.
			// Null-terminate it temporarily here so that we can work
			// with it.
			*p = '\0';
			if (stat(src, &s) == 0 && S_ISDIR(s.st_mode)) {
				// Null-terminate the dst path and undo its previous
				// termination.
				*q = '\0';
				*r = '/';
				r = q;
				if (mkdir(dst, 0700) != 0 && errno != EEXIST)

				if (chmod(dst, s.st_mode) != 0)

			}
			if (!last) {
				// If we're not at the final terminating null, restore
				// the slash so that we can continue our traversal.

static void sixpack_close(struct tty_struct *tty)
{
	struct sixpack *sp;

	write_lock_irq(&disc_data_lock);
	sp = tty->disc_data;
	tty->disc_data = NULL;
	write_unlock_irq(&disc_data_lock);
	if (!sp)
		return;

	/*
	 * We have now ensured that nobody can start using ap from now on, but
	 * we have to wait for all existing users to finish.
	 */
	if (!refcount_dec_and_test(&sp->refcnt))
		wait_for_completion(&sp->dead);

	/* We must stop the queue to avoid potentially scribbling
	 * on the free buffers. The sp->dead completion is not sufficient
	 * to protect us from sp->xbuff access.
	 */
	netif_stop_queue(sp->dev);

	del_timer_sync(&sp->tx_t);
	del_timer_sync(&sp->resync_t);

	unregister_netdev(sp->dev);

	/* Free all 6pack frame buffers after unreg. */
	kfree(sp->rbuff);
	kfree(sp->xbuff);

	free_netdev(sp->dev);
}

struct vfsmount *clone_private_mount(const struct path *path)
{
	struct mount *old_mnt = real_mount(path->mnt);
	struct mount *new_mnt;

	if (IS_MNT_UNBINDABLE(old_mnt))
		goto invalid;

	if (!check_mnt(old_mnt))
		goto invalid;

	if (has_locked_children(old_mnt, path->dentry))
		goto invalid;

	new_mnt = clone_mnt(old_mnt, path->dentry, CL_PRIVATE);
	up_read(&namespace_sem);

	if (IS_ERR(new_mnt))
		return ERR_CAST(new_mnt);

	/* Longterm mount to be removed by kern_unmount*() */
	new_mnt->mnt_ns = MNT_NS_INTERNAL;

	return &new_mnt->mnt;

	up_read(&namespace_sem);
	return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);
}

static int io_rw_init_file(struct io_kiocb *req, fmode_t mode)
{
	struct kiocb *kiocb = &req->rw.kiocb;
	struct io_ring_ctx *ctx = req->ctx;
	struct file *file = req->file;
	int ret;

	if (unlikely(!file || !(file->f_mode & mode)))
		return -EBADF;

	if (!io_req_ffs_set(req))
		req->flags |= io_file_get_flags(file) << REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT_BIT;

	kiocb->ki_flags = iocb_flags(file);
	ret = kiocb_set_rw_flags(kiocb, req->rw.flags);
	if (unlikely(ret))
		return ret;

	/*
	 * If the file is marked O_NONBLOCK, still allow retry for it if it
	 * supports async. Otherwise it's impossible to use O_NONBLOCK files
	 * reliably. If not, or it IOCB_NOWAIT is set, don't retry.
	 */
	if ((kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_NOWAIT) ||
	    ((file->f_flags & O_NONBLOCK) && !io_file_supports_nowait(req)))
		req->flags |= REQ_F_NOWAIT;

	if (ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL) {
		if (!(kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_DIRECT) || !file->f_op->iopoll)
			return -EOPNOTSUPP;

		kiocb->ki_flags |= IOCB_HIPRI | IOCB_ALLOC_CACHE;
		kiocb->ki_complete = io_complete_rw_iopoll;
		req->iopoll_completed = 0;
	} else {
		if (kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_HIPRI)
			return -EINVAL;
		kiocb->ki_complete = io_complete_rw;
	}

	return 0;
}

static void sixpack_close(struct tty_struct *tty)
{
	struct sixpack *sp;

	write_lock_irq(&disc_data_lock);
	sp = tty->disc_data;
	tty->disc_data = NULL;
	write_unlock_irq(&disc_data_lock);
	if (!sp)
		return;

	/*
	 * We have now ensured that nobody can start using ap from now on, but
	 * we have to wait for all existing users to finish.
	 */
	if (!refcount_dec_and_test(&sp->refcnt))
		wait_for_completion(&sp->dead);

	/* We must stop the queue to avoid potentially scribbling
	 * on the free buffers. The sp->dead completion is not sufficient
	 * to protect us from sp->xbuff access.
	 */
	netif_stop_queue(sp->dev);

	unregister_netdev(sp->dev);

	del_timer_sync(&sp->tx_t);
	del_timer_sync(&sp->resync_t);

	/* Free all 6pack frame buffers after unreg. */
	kfree(sp->rbuff);
	kfree(sp->xbuff);

	free_netdev(sp->dev);
}

static int __io_sync_cancel(struct io_uring_task *tctx,
			    struct io_cancel_data *cd, int fd)
{
	struct io_ring_ctx *ctx = cd->ctx;

	/* fixed must be grabbed every time since we drop the uring_lock */
	if ((cd->flags & IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD) &&
	    (cd->flags & IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD_FIXED)) {
		unsigned long file_ptr;

		if (unlikely(fd > ctx->nr_user_files))
			return -EBADF;
		fd = array_index_nospec(fd, ctx->nr_user_files);
		file_ptr = io_fixed_file_slot(&ctx->file_table, fd)->file_ptr;
		cd->file = (struct file *) (file_ptr & FFS_MASK);
		if (!cd->file)
			return -EBADF;
	}

	return __io_async_cancel(cd, tctx, 0);
}

static void parse_rtcp_bye(pjmedia_rtcp_session *sess,
			   const void *pkt,
			   pj_size_t size)
{

                             *((pj_uint8_t*)pkt+8));
	pj_memcpy(sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_, ((pj_uint8_t*)pkt+9),
		  reason.slen);
	reason.ptr = sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_;
    }

    /* Just print RTCP BYE log */
    PJ_LOG(5, (sess->name, "Received RTCP BYE, reason: %.*s",
	       reason.slen, reason.ptr));

MEMORY SAFETY:

NUMERIC SAFETY:
- Integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190): Arithmetic on sizes or counts that wraps and is then used for allocation, comparison, or indexing.
- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.

- Missing verification (CWE-347): Not verifying signatures, certificates, or MACs.

- Race condition (CWE-362/367): Shared state modified without proper synchronization, or TOCTOU between check and use.

gpg_ctx_add_recipient (struct _GpgCtx *gpg,
                       const gchar *keyid)
{
	gchar *safe_keyid;

	if (gpg->mode != GPG_CTX_MODE_ENCRYPT && gpg->mode != GPG_CTX_MODE_EXPORT)
		return;

	if (!gpg->recipients)
		gpg->recipients = g_ptr_array_new ();

	g_return_if_fail (keyid != NULL);

	/* If the recipient looks like an email address,
	 * enclose it in brackets to ensure an exact match. */
	if (strchr (keyid, '@') != NULL) {
		safe_keyid = g_strdup_printf ("<%s>", keyid);
	} else {
		safe_keyid = g_strdup (keyid);
	}

	g_ptr_array_add (gpg->recipients, safe_keyid);
}

struct sctp_chunk *sctp_make_strreset_req(
					const struct sctp_association *asoc,
					__u16 stream_num, __be16 *stream_list,
					bool out, bool in)
{
	__u16 stream_len = stream_num * sizeof(__u16);
	struct sctp_strreset_outreq outreq;
	struct sctp_strreset_inreq inreq;
	struct sctp_chunk *retval;
	__u16 outlen, inlen;

	outlen = (sizeof(outreq) + stream_len) * out;
	inlen = (sizeof(inreq) + stream_len) * in;

	retval = sctp_make_reconf(asoc, SCTP_PAD4(outlen) + SCTP_PAD4(inlen));
	if (!retval)
		return NULL;

	if (outlen) {
		outreq.param_hdr.type = SCTP_PARAM_RESET_OUT_REQUEST;
		outreq.param_hdr.length = htons(outlen);
		outreq.request_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_outseq);
		outreq.response_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_inseq - 1);
		outreq.send_reset_at_tsn = htonl(asoc->next_tsn - 1);

		sctp_addto_chunk(retval, sizeof(outreq), &outreq);

		if (stream_len)
			sctp_addto_chunk(retval, stream_len, stream_list);
	}

	if (inlen) {
		inreq.param_hdr.type = SCTP_PARAM_RESET_IN_REQUEST;
		inreq.param_hdr.length = htons(inlen);
		inreq.request_seq = htonl(asoc->strreset_outseq + out);

		sctp_addto_chunk(retval, sizeof(inreq), &inreq);

		if (stream_len)
			sctp_addto_chunk(retval, stream_len, stream_list);
	}

	return retval;
}

static int io_rw_init_file(struct io_kiocb *req, fmode_t mode)
{
	struct kiocb *kiocb = &req->rw.kiocb;
	struct io_ring_ctx *ctx = req->ctx;
	struct file *file = req->file;
	int ret;

	if (unlikely(!file || !(file->f_mode & mode)))
		return -EBADF;

	if (!io_req_ffs_set(req))
		req->flags |= io_file_get_flags(file) << REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT_BIT;

	kiocb->ki_flags = iocb_flags(file);
	ret = kiocb_set_rw_flags(kiocb, req->rw.flags);
	if (unlikely(ret))
		return ret;

	/*
	 * If the file is marked O_NONBLOCK, still allow retry for it if it
	 * supports async. Otherwise it's impossible to use O_NONBLOCK files
	 * reliably. If not, or it IOCB_NOWAIT is set, don't retry.
	 */
	if ((kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_NOWAIT) ||
	    ((file->f_flags & O_NONBLOCK) && !io_file_supports_nowait(req)))
		req->flags |= REQ_F_NOWAIT;

	if (ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL) {
		if (!(kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_DIRECT) || !file->f_op->iopoll)
			return -EOPNOTSUPP;

		kiocb->private = NULL;
		kiocb->ki_flags |= IOCB_HIPRI | IOCB_ALLOC_CACHE;
		kiocb->ki_complete = io_complete_rw_iopoll;
		req->iopoll_completed = 0;
	} else {
		if (kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_HIPRI)
			return -EINVAL;
		kiocb->ki_complete = io_complete_rw;
	}

	return 0;
}

    // Allocate LWPolyline vertices (group code 90):
    if (groupCode==90) {
        maxVertices = toInt(groupValue);

            if (vertices!=NULL) {
                delete[] vertices;
            }
            vertices = new double[4*maxVertices];
            for (int i=0; i<maxVertices; ++i) {
                vertices[i*4] = 0.0;
                vertices[i*4+1] = 0.0;
                vertices[i*4+2] = 0.0;
                vertices[i*4+3] = 0.0;
            }
        }
        vertexIndex=-1;
        return true;
    }

    // Process LWPolylines vertices (group codes 10/20/30/42):

        if (vertexIndex<maxVertices-1 && groupCode==10) {

            if (vertexIndex>=0 && vertexIndex<maxVertices) {
                vertices[4*vertexIndex + (groupCode/10-1)] = toReal(groupValue);

void add_interrupt_randomness(int irq, int irq_flags)
{
	struct entropy_store	*r;
	struct fast_pool	*fast_pool = this_cpu_ptr(&irq_randomness);
	struct pt_regs		*regs = get_irq_regs();
	unsigned long		now = jiffies;
	cycles_t		cycles = random_get_entropy();
	__u32			c_high, j_high;
	__u64			ip;
	unsigned long		seed;
	int			credit = 0;

	if (cycles == 0)
		cycles = get_reg(fast_pool, regs);
	c_high = (sizeof(cycles) > 4) ? cycles >> 32 : 0;
	j_high = (sizeof(now) > 4) ? now >> 32 : 0;
	fast_pool->pool[0] ^= cycles ^ j_high ^ irq;
	fast_pool->pool[1] ^= now ^ c_high;
	ip = regs ? instruction_pointer(regs) : _RET_IP_;
	fast_pool->pool[2] ^= ip;
	fast_pool->pool[3] ^= (sizeof(ip) > 4) ? ip >> 32 :
		get_reg(fast_pool, regs);

	fast_mix(fast_pool);
	add_interrupt_bench(cycles);

	if (unlikely(crng_init == 0)) {
		if ((fast_pool->count >= 64) &&
		    crng_fast_load((char *) fast_pool->pool,
				   sizeof(fast_pool->pool))) {
			fast_pool->count = 0;
			fast_pool->last = now;
		}
		return;
	}

	if ((fast_pool->count < 64) &&
	    !time_after(now, fast_pool->last + HZ))
		return;

	r = &input_pool;
	if (!spin_trylock(&r->lock))
		return;

	fast_pool->last = now;
	__mix_pool_bytes(r, &fast_pool->pool, sizeof(fast_pool->pool));

	/*
	 * If we have architectural seed generator, produce a seed and
	 * add it to the pool.  For the sake of paranoia don't let the
	 * architectural seed generator dominate the input from the
	 * interrupt noise.
	 */
	if (arch_get_random_seed_long(&seed)) {
		__mix_pool_bytes(r, &seed, sizeof(seed));
		credit = 1;
	}
	spin_unlock(&r->lock);

	fast_pool->count = 0;

	/* award one bit for the contents of the fast pool */
	credit_entropy_bits(r, credit + 1);
}

static size_t push_pipe(struct iov_iter *i, size_t size,
			int *iter_headp, size_t *offp)
{
	struct pipe_inode_info *pipe = i->pipe;
	unsigned int p_tail = pipe->tail;
	unsigned int p_mask = pipe->ring_size - 1;
	unsigned int iter_head;
	size_t off;
	ssize_t left;

	if (unlikely(size > i->count))
		size = i->count;
	if (unlikely(!size))
		return 0;

	left = size;
	data_start(i, &iter_head, &off);
	*iter_headp = iter_head;
	*offp = off;
	if (off) {
		left -= PAGE_SIZE - off;
		if (left <= 0) {
			pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask].len += size;
			return size;
		}
		pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask].len = PAGE_SIZE;
		iter_head++;
	}
	while (!pipe_full(iter_head, p_tail, pipe->max_usage)) {
		struct pipe_buffer *buf = &pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask];
		struct page *page = alloc_page(GFP_USER);
		if (!page)
			break;

		buf->ops = &default_pipe_buf_ops;
		buf->page = page;
		buf->offset = 0;
		buf->len = min_t(ssize_t, left, PAGE_SIZE);
		left -= buf->len;
		iter_head++;
		pipe->head = iter_head;

static size_t push_pipe(struct iov_iter *i, size_t size,
			int *iter_headp, size_t *offp)
{
	struct pipe_inode_info *pipe = i->pipe;
	unsigned int p_tail = pipe->tail;
	unsigned int p_mask = pipe->ring_size - 1;
	unsigned int iter_head;
	size_t off;
	ssize_t left;

	if (unlikely(size > i->count))
		size = i->count;
	if (unlikely(!size))
		return 0;

	left = size;
	data_start(i, &iter_head, &off);
	*iter_headp = iter_head;
	*offp = off;
	if (off) {
		left -= PAGE_SIZE - off;
		if (left <= 0) {
			pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask].len += size;
			return size;
		}
		pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask].len = PAGE_SIZE;
		iter_head++;
	}
	while (!pipe_full(iter_head, p_tail, pipe->max_usage)) {
		struct pipe_buffer *buf = &pipe->bufs[iter_head & p_mask];
		struct page *page = alloc_page(GFP_USER);
		if (!page)
			break;

		buf->ops = &default_pipe_buf_ops;
		buf->flags = 0;
		buf->page = page;
		buf->offset = 0;
		buf->len = min_t(ssize_t, left, PAGE_SIZE);
		left -= buf->len;
		iter_head++;
		pipe->head = iter_head;

		if (left == 0)
			return size;
	}
	return size - left;
}

void update_process_times(int user_tick)
{
	struct task_struct *p = current;

	/* Note: this timer irq context must be accounted for as well. */
	account_process_tick(p, user_tick);
	run_local_timers();
	rcu_sched_clock_irq(user_tick);
#ifdef CONFIG_IRQ_WORK
	if (in_irq())
		irq_work_tick();
#endif
	scheduler_tick();
	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_POSIX_TIMERS))
		run_posix_cpu_timers();

	/* The current CPU might make use of net randoms without receiving IRQs
	 * to renew them often enough. Let's update the net_rand_state from a
	 * non-constant value that's not affine to the number of calls to make
	 * sure it's updated when there's some activity (we don't care in idle).
	 */
	this_cpu_add(net_rand_state.s1, rol32(jiffies, 24) + user_tick);
}

void add_interrupt_randomness(int irq, int irq_flags)
{
	struct entropy_store	*r;
	struct fast_pool	*fast_pool = this_cpu_ptr(&irq_randomness);
	struct pt_regs		*regs = get_irq_regs();
	unsigned long		now = jiffies;
	cycles_t		cycles = random_get_entropy();
	__u32			c_high, j_high;
	__u64			ip;
	unsigned long		seed;
	int			credit = 0;

	if (cycles == 0)
		cycles = get_reg(fast_pool, regs);
	c_high = (sizeof(cycles) > 4) ? cycles >> 32 : 0;
	j_high = (sizeof(now) > 4) ? now >> 32 : 0;
	fast_pool->pool[0] ^= cycles ^ j_high ^ irq;
	fast_pool->pool[1] ^= now ^ c_high;
	ip = regs ? instruction_pointer(regs) : _RET_IP_;
	fast_pool->pool[2] ^= ip;
	fast_pool->pool[3] ^= (sizeof(ip) > 4) ? ip >> 32 :
		get_reg(fast_pool, regs);

	fast_mix(fast_pool);
	add_interrupt_bench(cycles);
	this_cpu_add(net_rand_state.s1, fast_pool->pool[cycles & 3]);

	if (unlikely(crng_init == 0)) {
		if ((fast_pool->count >= 64) &&
		    crng_fast_load((char *) fast_pool->pool,
				   sizeof(fast_pool->pool))) {
			fast_pool->count = 0;
			fast_pool->last = now;
		}
		return;
	}

	if ((fast_pool->count < 64) &&
	    !time_after(now, fast_pool->last + HZ))
		return;

	r = &input_pool;
	if (!spin_trylock(&r->lock))
		return;

	fast_pool->last = now;
	__mix_pool_bytes(r, &fast_pool->pool, sizeof(fast_pool->pool));

	/*
	 * If we have architectural seed generator, produce a seed and
	 * add it to the pool.  For the sake of paranoia don't let the
	 * architectural seed generator dominate the input from the
	 * interrupt noise.
	 */
	if (arch_get_random_seed_long(&seed)) {
		__mix_pool_bytes(r, &seed, sizeof(seed));
		credit = 1;
	}
	spin_unlock(&r->lock);

	fast_pool->count = 0;

	/* award one bit for the contents of the fast pool */
	credit_entropy_bits(r, credit + 1);
}

1. When `n1` comes from `get_st32` (signed 32-bit cast to `ut32`), a negative value becomes a huge unsigned value. `malloc(n1 + 1)` could wrap to 0 when n1 is `0xFFFFFFFF` (i.e., -1 as st32), allocating a small buffer but then reading a huge amount.

For issue 1: `get_st32` returns a signed 32-bit value stored into `ut32 n1`. If `get_st32` returns -1 (0xFFFFFFFF as ut32), then `n1 + 1 = 0`, so `malloc(0)` returns a small/valid pointer or NULL. If non-NULL, `rz_buf_read(buffer, s1, 0xFFFFFFFF)` would attempt to read ~4GB. The size check `size != n1` would likely catch this since the buffer won't have that much data. So the overflow leading to heap overflow is blocked by the size check in practice for extreme values.

But consider `n1 = 0xFFFFFFFF`: `malloc(0)` → small allocation, `rz_buf_read` with size `0xFFFFFFFF` → could write past the buffer before returning a short read. The damage depends on `rz_buf_read` behavior, but typically `rz_buf_read` could write some bytes before stopping, causing a heap buffer overflow.

Concrete trigger: `pyc->magic_int & 0xffff > 62061`, buffer contains bytes making `get_st32` return `-1` (0xFFFFFFFF as ut32). `malloc(0+1)` wait, `0xFFFFFFFF + 1 = 0`, `malloc(0)`. Then `rz_buf_read(buffer, s1, 0xFFFFFFFF)` writes to a 0-sized (or minimally sized) buffer.

This is CWE-190 (integer overflow) leading to CWE-787 (heap buffer overflow).

static ssize_t remove_slot_store(struct kobject *kobj,
				 struct kobj_attribute *attr,
				 const char *buf, size_t nbytes)
{
	char drc_name[MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN];
	int rc;
	char *end;

	if (nbytes >= MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN)
		return 0;

	memcpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes);

	end = strchr(drc_name, '\n');
	if (!end)

Your task: analyze the code and determine whether it is VULNERABLE or NOT VULNERABLE.

Use Structured Chain-of-Thought (SCoT) reasoning with explicit program structures (Sequence, Branch, Loop) across the following phases:

=== PHASE 1: CODE COMPREHENSION ===
Trace the code using SCoT structures to build a complete model of behavior.

Sequence: Trace the code step by step. Identify:
  - All inputs (parameters, global state, return values from called functions, data read from buffers/network/files)
  - All outputs (return values, written buffers, side effects)
  - All type conversions and arithmetic operations on sizes, indices, offsets, or lengths
  - All resource lifecycle operations (alloc/free, open/close, lock/unlock, init/cleanup)

Branch: Map every conditional path. For EACH branch, document:
  - The exact condition expression and its operator (pay attention to > vs >=, < vs <=, == vs !=)
  - What happens on the true path vs. the false path
  - Whether the branch is a SAFETY GUARD (bounds check, NULL check, error check, validation)

Loop: For each loop, identify:
  - What controls iteration count or termination
  - Whether an attacker can influence iteration count or loop body behavior
  - What data is accessed per iteration and whether indices stay in bounds

=== PHASE 2: DEFENSE INVENTORY ===
Before looking for vulnerabilities, catalog every defensive measure in the code:

For each safety guard found in Phase 1, record:
  1. GUARD LOCATION: exact line/expression
  2. GUARD TYPE: bounds check, NULL check, error return check, input validation, length limit, permission check, sanitization
  3. PROTECTED OPERATION: what specific downstream operation this guard protects
  4. COMPLETENESS: does the guard fully prevent the dangerous condition? Check:
     - Does it use the correct comparison operator? (> vs >=, < vs <=)
     - Does it check the SAME variable used in the protected operation?
     - Does the guard cover ALL paths to the protected operation? (no alternate unguarded path?)
     - On the error path, does execution STOP (return/break/goto cleanup) or does it fall through?
  5. VERDICT: EFFECTIVE (fully prevents the issue) or INCOMPLETE (gap identified, state what gap)

=== PHASE 3: VULNERABILITY HYPOTHESIS ===
Systematically check each vulnerability class below. For each class, determine whether the code contains that pattern. Cite specific lines or expressions.

MEMORY SAFETY:
- Buffer overflow/out-of-bounds write (CWE-787/120/121/122): Write past buffer bounds. Check all memcpy, strcpy, strncpy, sprintf, array indexing with attacker-influenced index or size. Check if length/size parameters are validated BEFORE the copy/write.
- Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): Read past buffer bounds. Check array accesses, pointer arithmetic with external indices.
- Use-after-free (CWE-416) / Double-free (CWE-415): Memory accessed or freed after it was already freed. Check all paths through error handling and cleanup.
- Uninitialized variable use (CWE-457/908): Variable declared but not assigned on all paths before use, especially in security-critical computation.

NUMERIC SAFETY:
- Integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190): Arithmetic on sizes or counts that wraps and is then used for allocation, comparison, or indexing.
- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.
- Type confusion / truncation (CWE-681/197): A value stored in a wider type is narrowed, and the truncation changes the value used in a security-critical operation.

POINTER/REFERENCE SAFETY:
- NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476): A function returns NULL on error, and the code does not check before dereferencing.
- Missing error check leading to unsafe state (CWE-252/390): A function returns an error code or NULL, and the code either does not check or checks but does NOT stop execution afterward.

INPUT VALIDATION:
- Command injection (CWE-78), SQL injection (CWE-89), Path traversal (CWE-22), Format string (CWE-134), Log injection (CWE-117), HTTP header injection (CWE-113), SSRF (CWE-918), XPath/LDAP/XML injection (CWE-643/90/91), Code injection (CWE-94).
- For SSRF/injection: commented-out or disabled validation counts as missing validation.

CRYPTOGRAPHY:
- Weak key size (CWE-326): RSA < 2048 bits, DSA < 2048 bits, EC < 224 bits, symmetric < 128 bits.
- Broken/risky algorithm (CWE-327/328): MD5, SHA1 for security purposes, DES, RC4, ECB mode.
- Weak randomness (CWE-330/338): Using rand(), random(), or predictable seeds for security-critical values.
- Missing verification (CWE-347): Not verifying signatures, certificates, or MACs.

CONCURRENCY:
- Race condition (CWE-362/367): Shared state modified without proper synchronization, or TOCTOU between check and use.

AUTHORIZATION/ACCESS:
- Missing authorization (CWE-862/863): Security-sensitive operation without access control check.

RESOURCE MANAGEMENT:
- Uncontrolled resource consumption / ReDoS (CWE-400/1333): Regular expressions with catastrophic backtracking, unbounded allocation controlled by attacker.

=== PHASE 4: EVIDENCE VERIFICATION (MOST CRITICAL PHASE) ===
For each candidate vulnerability identified in Phase 3, apply ALL of the following checks. A finding must pass every check to survive.

STEP A — Construct a concrete trigger: Specify EXACT input values or program state that would trigger the vulnerability. You must name actual values for variables, buffer sizes, and indices. "An attacker-controlled value that is larger than the buffer" is NOT concrete. "Setting rsp->data[0] to 255 when the destination buffer is 64 bytes" IS concrete. If you cannot construct a concrete trigger using only information present in the code, the finding is SPECULATIVE. Mark it REJECTED.

STEP B — Verify against the defense inventory: Cross-reference your finding against EVERY guard cataloged in Phase 2.
  - If a guard was marked EFFECTIVE in Phase 2 and it protects the exact operation you are flagging, the finding is BLOCKED. Mark it REJECTED.
  - Only if you can demonstrate the guard is INCOMPLETE (and you identified the specific gap in Phase 2) can the finding survive.
  - CRITICAL: Do not find a vulnerability and then ignore a guard you already documented. If you documented a guard as EFFECTIVE, you cannot later claim the guarded operation is vulnerable without first explaining why your Phase 2 assessment was wrong.

STEP C — Path reachability: Trace a complete execution path from function entry to the vulnerable operation using your concrete trigger values from Step A. The path must pass through all conditionals correctly given those specific values. If any guard on the path would catch your trigger values, the finding is BLOCKED. Mark it REJECTED.

STEP D — Root cause identification: Identify the single root cause. If multiple symptoms stem from the same root cause, report only the root cause once. Map to the most specific CWE:
  - Missing bounds check before array access → CWE-787 (write) or CWE-125 (read)
  - Off-by-one in bounds check → CWE-193 leading to CWE-787 or CWE-125
  - Missing NULL check after allocation/lookup → CWE-476
  - Missing return/break after error detection → CWE-252 or CWE-390
  - Integer overflow used as size → CWE-190
  - Unsigned underflow in length → CWE-191
  - User input in format string → CWE-134
  - Weak key size → CWE-326
  - Disabled/commented-out input validation → the CWE for the attack that validation would prevent

  - Off-by-one claims where you have not verified the actual array allocation convention (0-indexed vs 1-indexed, whether size includes a sentinel element)
  - Resource leaks (memory, file descriptors) that have no security impact (no DoS amplification, no information disclosure). A simple memory leak is NOT a security vulnerability unless an attacker can trigger it repeatedly to exhaust resources.

  - Unsigned subtraction underflow where the operands are constrained by prior checks to prevent the underflow case
  - Race conditions in code that is architecturally single-threaded or where the lock scope matches the access scope

- vulnerable = true

- Cite the exact code location (line numbers and code snippet) for each finding
- Confidence reflects evidence strength: use 0.9+ only when you have a fully concrete trigger

If NO findings survived verification:
- vulnerable = false
- Confidence reflects analysis thoroughness

You are an expert software security auditor performing vulnerability detection. Your goal is to determine whether the given code contains a security vulnerability.

Your task: analyze the code and determine whether it is VULNERABLE or NOT VULNERABLE.

Use Structured Chain-of-Thought (SCoT) reasoning with explicit program structures (Sequence, Branch, Loop) across the following phases:

=== PHASE 1: CODE COMPREHENSION ===
Trace the code using SCoT structures to build a complete model of behavior.

Sequence: Trace the code step by step. Identify:
  - All inputs (parameters, global state, return values from called functions, data read from buffers/network/files)
  - All outputs (return values, written buffers, side effects)
  - All type conversions and arithmetic operations on sizes, indices, offsets, or lengths
  - All resource lifecycle operations (alloc/free, open/close, lock/unlock, init/cleanup)

Branch: Map every conditional path. For EACH branch, document:
  - The exact condition expression and its operator (pay attention to > vs >=, < vs <=, == vs !=)
  - What happens on the true path vs. the false path
  - Whether the branch is a SAFETY GUARD (bounds check, NULL check, error check, validation)

Loop: For each loop, identify:
  - What controls iteration count or termination
  - Whether an attacker can influence iteration count or loop body behavior
  - What data is accessed per iteration and whether indices stay in bounds

=== PHASE 2: DEFENSE INVENTORY ===
Before looking for vulnerabilities, catalog every defensive measure in the code:

For each safety guard found in Phase 1, record:
  1. GUARD LOCATION: exact line/expression
  2. GUARD TYPE: bounds check, NULL check, error return check, input validation, length limit, permission check, sanitization
  3. PROTECTED OPERATION: what specific downstream operation this guard protects
  4. COMPLETENESS: does the guard fully prevent the dangerous condition? Check:
     - Does it use the correct comparison operator? (> vs >=, < vs <=)
     - Does it check the SAME variable used in the protected operation?
     - Does the guard cover ALL paths to the protected operation? (no alternate unguarded path?)
     - On the error path, does execution STOP (return/break/goto cleanup) or does it fall through?
  5. VERDICT: EFFECTIVE (fully prevents the issue) or INCOMPLETE (gap identified, state what gap)

=== PHASE 3: VULNERABILITY HYPOTHESIS ===
Systematically check each vulnerability class below. For each class, determine whether the code contains that pattern. Cite specific lines or expressions.

MEMORY SAFETY:
- Buffer overflow/out-of-bounds write (CWE-787/120/121/122): Write past buffer bounds. Check all memcpy, strcpy, strncpy, sprintf, array indexing with attacker-influenced index or size. Check if length/size parameters are validated BEFORE the copy/write.
- Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): Read past buffer bounds. Check array accesses, pointer arithmetic with external indices.
- Use-after-free (CWE-416) / Double-free (CWE-415): Memory accessed or freed after it was already freed. Check all paths through error handling and cleanup.
- Uninitialized variable use (CWE-457/908): Variable declared but not assigned on all paths before use, especially in security-critical computation.

NUMERIC SAFETY:
- Integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190): Arithmetic on sizes or counts that wraps and is then used for allocation, comparison, or indexing.
- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.
- Type confusion / truncation (CWE-681/197): A value stored in a wider type is narrowed, and the truncation changes the value used in a security-critical operation.

POINTER/REFERENCE SAFETY:
- NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476): A function returns NULL on error, and the code does not check before dereferencing.
- Missing error check leading to unsafe state (CWE-252/390): A function returns an error code or NULL, and the code either does not check or checks but does NOT stop execution afterward.

INPUT VALIDATION:
- Command injection (CWE-78), SQL injection (CWE-89), Path traversal (CWE-22), Format string (CWE-134), Log injection (CWE-117), HTTP header injection (CWE-113), SSRF (CWE-918), XPath/LDAP/XML injection (CWE-643/90/91), Code injection (CWE-94).
- For SSRF/injection: commented-out or disabled validation counts as missing validation.

CRYPTOGRAPHY:
- Weak key size (CWE-326): RSA < 2048 bits, DSA < 2048 bits, EC < 224 bits, symmetric < 128 bits.
- Broken/risky algorithm (CWE-327/328): MD5, SHA1 for security purposes, DES, RC4, ECB mode.
- Weak randomness (CWE-330/338): Using rand(), random(), or predictable seeds for security-critical values.
- Missing verification (CWE-347): Not verifying signatures, certificates, or MACs.

CONCURRENCY:
- Race condition (CWE-362/367): Shared state modified without proper synchronization, or TOCTOU between check and use.

AUTHORIZATION/ACCESS:
- Missing authorization (CWE-862/863): Security-sensitive operation without access control check.

RESOURCE MANAGEMENT:
- Uncontrolled resource consumption / ReDoS (CWE-400/1333): Regular expressions with catastrophic backtracking, unbounded allocation controlled by attacker.

=== PHASE 4: EVIDENCE VERIFICATION (MOST CRITICAL PHASE) ===
For each candidate vulnerability identified in Phase 3, apply ALL of the following checks. A finding must pass every check to survive.

STEP A — Construct a concrete trigger: Specify EXACT input values or program state that would trigger the vulnerability. You must name actual values for variables, buffer sizes, and indices. "An attacker-controlled value that is larger than the buffer" is NOT concrete. "Setting rsp->data[0] to 255 when the destination buffer is 64 bytes" IS concrete. If you cannot construct a concrete trigger using only information present in the code, the finding is SPECULATIVE. Mark it REJECTED.

STEP B — Verify against the defense inventory: Cross-reference your finding against EVERY guard cataloged in Phase 2.
  - If a guard was marked EFFECTIVE in Phase 2 and it protects the exact operation you are flagging, the finding is BLOCKED. Mark it REJECTED.
  - Only if you can demonstrate the guard is INCOMPLETE (and you identified the specific gap in Phase 2) can the finding survive.
  - CRITICAL: Do not find a vulnerability and then ignore a guard you already documented. If you documented a guard as EFFECTIVE, you cannot later claim the guarded operation is vulnerable without first explaining why your Phase 2 assessment was wrong.

STEP C — Path reachability: Trace a complete execution path from function entry to the vulnerable operation using your concrete trigger values from Step A. The path must pass through all conditionals correctly given those specific values. If any guard on the path would catch your trigger values, the finding is BLOCKED. Mark it REJECTED.

STEP D — Root cause identification: Identify the single root cause. If multiple symptoms stem from the same root cause, report only the root cause once. Map to the most specific CWE:
  - Missing bounds check before array access → CWE-787 (write) or CWE-125 (read)
  - Off-by-one in bounds check → CWE-193 leading to CWE-787 or CWE-125
  - Missing NULL check after allocation/lookup → CWE-476
  - Missing return/break after error detection → CWE-252 or CWE-390
  - Integer overflow used as size → CWE-190
  - Unsigned underflow in length → CWE-191
  - User input in format string → CWE-134
  - Weak key size → CWE-326
  - Disabled/commented-out input validation → the CWE for the attack that validation would prevent

STEP E — Reject common false-positive patterns: A finding is REJECTED if it matches any of these patterns:
  - NULL pointer from standard framework/library functions where the API contract guarantees non-NULL in the calling context (e.g., internal callback parameters provided by the framework, iterator values during valid iteration)
  - Integer overflow/underflow that requires values outside the domain enforced by input parsing, protocol constraints, or earlier validation in the same function
  - Off-by-one claims where you have not verified the actual array allocation convention (0-indexed vs 1-indexed, whether size includes a sentinel element)
  - Resource leaks (memory, file descriptors) that have no security impact (no DoS amplification, no information disclosure). A simple memory leak is NOT a security vulnerability unless an attacker can trigger it repeatedly to exhaust resources.
  - Claiming a variable "might" or "could" be negative/NULL/large without demonstrating a concrete path that produces that value using the code shown
  - Unsigned subtraction underflow where the operands are constrained by prior checks to prevent the underflow case
  - Race conditions in code that is architecturally single-threaded or where the lock scope matches the access scope

=== PHASE 5: FINAL VERDICT ===
Based on surviving evidence from Phase 4:

If one or more findings survived ALL verification steps:
- vulnerable = true
- Report the CWE(s) only for verified finding(s), using the most specific CWE from Step D
- Cite the exact code location (line numbers and code snippet) for each finding
- Confidence reflects evidence strength: use 0.9+ only when you have a fully concrete trigger

If NO findings survived verification:
- vulnerable = false
- Confidence reflects analysis thoroughness

Rules:
- Base analysis on the provided code. For called functions not shown, apply standard API contracts and reasonable assumptions about their behavior.
- A vulnerability must be reachable through a concrete execution path with concrete trigger values.
- Code that properly handles errors (checks return values AND stops execution on error) is NOT vulnerable for that error path.
- Do NOT count the same root cause multiple times.
- After your reasoning, you MUST output the JSON object below. Do not omit it.

Output format:
- First: write your SCoT reasoning following Phases 1-5 above.
- Then: output ONLY one JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text before or after the JSON).

Required JSON schema:
{
  "verdict": {
    "vulnerable": true/false,
    "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
    "cwe": ["CWE-..."],
    "severity": "low|medium|high|critical|unknown",
    "summary": "..."
  },
  "evidence": [
    {

      "snippet": "...",
      "reason": "..."
    }
  ],
  "notes": {

static struct rpmsg_device *rpmsg_virtio_add_ctrl_dev(struct virtio_device *vdev)
{
	struct virtproc_info *vrp = vdev->priv;
	struct virtio_rpmsg_channel *vch;
	struct rpmsg_device *rpdev_ctrl;
	int err = 0;

	vch = kzalloc(sizeof(*vch), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!vch)
		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);

	/* Link the channel to the vrp */
	vch->vrp = vrp;

	/* Assign public information to the rpmsg_device */
	rpdev_ctrl = &vch->rpdev;
	rpdev_ctrl->ops = &virtio_rpmsg_ops;

	rpdev_ctrl->dev.parent = &vrp->vdev->dev;
	rpdev_ctrl->dev.release = virtio_rpmsg_release_device;
	rpdev_ctrl->little_endian = virtio_is_little_endian(vrp->vdev);

	err = rpmsg_ctrldev_register_device(rpdev_ctrl);
	if (err) {
		kfree(vch);
		return ERR_PTR(err);
	}

	return rpdev_ctrl;
}

static struct rpmsg_device *rpmsg_virtio_add_ctrl_dev(struct virtio_device *vdev)
{
	struct virtproc_info *vrp = vdev->priv;
	struct virtio_rpmsg_channel *vch;

	if (err) {
		/* vch will be free in virtio_rpmsg_release_device() */
		return ERR_PTR(err);
	}

}

int cx23888_ir_probe(struct cx23885_dev *dev)
{
	struct cx23888_ir_state *state;
	struct v4l2_subdev *sd;
	struct v4l2_subdev_ir_parameters default_params;
	int ret;

	state = kzalloc(sizeof(struct cx23888_ir_state), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (state == NULL)
		return -ENOMEM;

	spin_lock_init(&state->rx_kfifo_lock);
	if (kfifo_alloc(&state->rx_kfifo, CX23888_IR_RX_KFIFO_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL))
		return -ENOMEM;

	state->dev = dev;
	sd = &state->sd;

	v4l2_subdev_init(sd, &cx23888_ir_controller_ops);
	v4l2_set_subdevdata(sd, state);
	/* FIXME - fix the formatting of dev->v4l2_dev.name and use it */
	snprintf(sd->name, sizeof(sd->name), "%s/888-ir", dev->name);
	sd->grp_id = CX23885_HW_888_IR;

	ret = v4l2_device_register_subdev(&dev->v4l2_dev, sd);
	if (ret == 0) {
		/*
		 * Ensure no interrupts arrive from '888 specific conditions,
		 * since we ignore them in this driver to have commonality with
		 * similar IR controller cores.
		 */
		cx23888_ir_write4(dev, CX23888_IR_IRQEN_REG, 0);

		mutex_init(&state->rx_params_lock);
		default_params = default_rx_params;
		v4l2_subdev_call(sd, ir, rx_s_parameters, &default_params);

		mutex_init(&state->tx_params_lock);
		default_params = default_tx_params;
		v4l2_subdev_call(sd, ir, tx_s_parameters, &default_params);
	} else {
		kfifo_free(&state->rx_kfifo);
	}
	return ret;
}

void jfs_evict_inode(struct inode *inode)
{

		}
	} else {
		truncate_inode_pages_final(&inode->i_data);
	}

	dquot_drop(inode);

	BUG_ON(!list_empty(&ji->anon_inode_list));

	if (ji->active_ag != -1) {
		struct bmap *bmap = JFS_SBI(inode->i_sb)->bmap;
		atomic_dec(&bmap->db_active[ji->active_ag]);
		ji->active_ag = -1;
	}

void *memslot_get_virt(RedMemSlotInfo *info, QXLPHYSICAL addr, uint32_t add_size,
                       int group_id)
{
    int slot_id;
    int generation;
    unsigned long h_virt;

    MemSlot *slot;

    if (group_id > info->num_memslots_groups) {
        spice_critical("group_id too big");
        return NULL;
    }

    slot_id = memslot_get_id(info, addr);
    if (slot_id > info->num_memslots) {
        print_memslots(info);
        spice_critical("slot_id %d too big, addr=%" PRIx64, slot_id, addr);
        return NULL;
    }

    slot = &info->mem_slots[group_id][slot_id];

    generation = memslot_get_generation(info, addr);
    if (generation != slot->generation) {
        print_memslots(info);
        spice_critical("address generation is not valid, group_id %d, slot_id %d, "
                       "gen %d, slot_gen %d",
                       group_id, slot_id,
                       generation, slot->generation);
        return NULL;
    }

    h_virt = __get_clean_virt(info, addr);
    h_virt += slot->address_delta;

    if (!memslot_validate_virt(info, h_virt, slot_id, add_size, group_id)) {
        return NULL;
    }

    return (void*)(uintptr_t)h_virt;
}

_fr_window_ask_overwrite_dialog (OverwriteData *odata)
{
	if ((odata->edata->overwrite == FR_OVERWRITE_ASK) && (odata->current_file != NULL)) {
		const char *base_name;
		GFile      *destination;

		base_name = _g_path_get_relative_basename ((char *) odata->current_file->data, odata->edata->base_dir, odata->edata->junk_paths);
		destination = g_file_get_child (odata->edata->destination, base_name);
		g_file_query_info_async (destination,
					 G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_TYPE "," G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_NAME "," G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_DISPLAY_NAME,
					 G_FILE_QUERY_INFO_NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS,
					 G_PRIORITY_DEFAULT,
					 odata->window->priv->cancellable,
					 query_info_ready_for_overwrite_dialog_cb,
					 odata);

		g_object_unref (destination);

		return;
	}

	if (odata->edata->file_list != NULL) {
		/* speed optimization: passing NULL when extracting all the
		 * files is faster if the command supports the
		 * propCanExtractAll property. */
		if (odata->extract_all) {
			_g_string_list_free (odata->edata->file_list);
			odata->edata->file_list = NULL;
		}
		odata->edata->overwrite = FR_OVERWRITE_YES;
		_fr_window_archive_extract_from_edata (odata->window, odata->edata);
	}
	else {
		GtkWidget *d;

		d = _gtk_message_dialog_new (GTK_WINDOW (odata->window),
					     0,
					     GTK_STOCK_DIALOG_WARNING,
					     _("Extraction not performed"),
					     NULL,
					     GTK_STOCK_OK, GTK_RESPONSE_OK,
					     NULL);
		gtk_dialog_set_default_response (GTK_DIALOG (d), GTK_RESPONSE_OK);
		fr_window_show_error_dialog (odata->window, d, GTK_WINDOW (odata->window), _("Extraction not performed"));

		fr_window_stop_batch (odata->window);
	}

	g_free (odata);
}

{
    char *logFileName = NULL;

    /* the format string below is controlled by the user,
       this code should never be called with elevated privileges */

        FatalError("Cannot allocate space for the log file name\n");

        struct stat buf;

        if (!stat(logFileName, &buf) && S_ISREG(buf.st_mode)) {
            char *suffix;
            char *oldLog;

            if ((asprintf(&suffix, backup, idstring) == -1) ||
                (asprintf(&oldLog, "%s%s", logFileName, suffix) == -1)) {
                FatalError("Cannot allocate space for the log file name\n");
            }
            free(suffix);

            if (rename(logFileName, oldLog) == -1) {
                FatalError("Cannot move old log file \"%s\" to \"%s\"\n",
                           logFileName, oldLog);
            }
            free(oldLog);
        }
    }
    else {
        if (remove(logFileName) != 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
            FatalError("Cannot remove old log file \"%s\": %s\n",
                       logFileName, strerror(errno));
        }
    }

LogFilePrep(const char *fname, const char *backup, const char *idstring)
{
    char *logFileName = NULL;

    if (asprintf(&logFileName, fname, idstring) == -1)
        FatalError("Cannot allocate space for the log file name\n");

    if (backup && *backup) {
        struct stat buf;

        if (!stat(logFileName, &buf) && S_ISREG(buf.st_mode)) {
            char *suffix;
            char *oldLog;

            if ((asprintf(&suffix, backup, idstring) == -1) ||
                (asprintf(&oldLog, "%s%s", logFileName, suffix) == -1)) {
                FatalError("Cannot allocate space for the log file name\n");
            }
            free(suffix);

            if (rename(logFileName, oldLog) == -1) {
                FatalError("Cannot move old log file \"%s\" to \"%s\"\n",
                           logFileName, oldLog);
            }
            free(oldLog);
        }
    }
    else {
        if (remove(logFileName) != 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
            FatalError("Cannot remove old log file \"%s\": %s\n",
                       logFileName, strerror(errno));
        }
    }

    return logFileName;
}

```c

```

If the first `asprintf` succeeds but the second fails, `suffix` is allocated but not freed before `FatalError`. That's just a minor leak on a fatal path.

But if the first `asprintf` **fails**, due to short-circuit evaluation, the second isn't called, and `FatalError` is invoked. That's fine.

No real security vulnerability here. The format string usage is by design with controlled parameters.

- Use-after-free (CWE-416) / Double-free (CWE-415): Memory accessed or freed after it was already freed. Check all paths through error handling and cleanup.

NUMERIC SAFETY:
- Integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190): Arithmetic on sizes or counts that wraps and is then used for allocation, comparison, or indexing.
- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.
- Type confusion / truncation (CWE-681/197): A value stored in a wider type is narrowed, and the truncation changes the value used in a security-critical operation.

- Missing verification (CWE-347): Not verifying signatures, certificates, or MACs.

- Race condition (CWE-362/367): Shared state modified without proper synchronization, or TOCTOU between check and use.

static size_t handle_returned_header (void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, void *stream)
{
    auth_client *auth_user = stream;
    size_t bytes = size * nmemb;
    client_t *client = auth_user->client;

    if (client)
    {

        auth_url *url = auth->state;

            char *eol;
            snprintf (url->errormsg, sizeof (url->errormsg), "%s", (char*)ptr+22);
            eol = strchr (url->errormsg, '\r');
            if (eol == NULL)

         newsize = target->len + add_len + 1;

int hfsplus_find_cat(struct super_block *sb, u32 cnid,
		     struct hfs_find_data *fd)
{
	hfsplus_cat_entry tmp;
	int err;
	u16 type;

	hfsplus_cat_build_key(sb, fd->search_key, cnid, NULL);
	err = hfs_brec_read(fd, &tmp, sizeof(hfsplus_cat_entry));
	if (err)
		return err;

	type = be16_to_cpu(tmp.type);
	if (type != HFSPLUS_FOLDER_THREAD && type != HFSPLUS_FILE_THREAD) {
		printk(KERN_ERR "hfs: found bad thread record in catalog\n");
		return -EIO;
	}

	if (be16_to_cpu(tmp.thread.nodeName.length) > 255) {
		printk(KERN_ERR "hfs: catalog name length corrupted\n");
		return -EIO;
	}

	hfsplus_cat_build_key_uni(fd->search_key, be32_to_cpu(tmp.thread.parentID),
				 &tmp.thread.nodeName);
	return hfs_brec_find(fd);
}

**Phase 3-4 Focus: Integer overflow in buffer size calculations**

In the `ReadStripMethod` case:
```c
extent=4*((image->depth+7)/8)*(samples_per_pixel+1)*TIFFStripSize(tiff);
```

All factors are attacker-controlled through the TIFF file. The multiplication can wrap around `size_t`, producing a small `extent`. === PHASE 1: CODE COMPREHENSION ===
Trace the code using SCoT structures to build a complete model of behavior.

Sequence: Trace the code step by step. Identify:
  - All inputs (parameters, global state, return values from called functions, data read from buffers/network/files)
  - All outputs (return values, written buffers, side effects)
  - All type conversions and arithmetic operations on sizes, indices, offsets, or lengths

- Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): Read past buffer bounds. Check array accesses, pointer arithmetic with external indices.
- Use-after-free (CWE-416) / Double-free (CWE-415): Memory accessed or freed after it was already freed. Check all paths through error handling and cleanup.
- Uninitialized variable use (CWE-457/908): Variable declared but not assigned on all paths before use, especially in security-critical computation.

NUMERIC SAFETY:
- Integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190): Arithmetic on sizes or counts that wraps and is then used for allocation, comparison, or indexing.
- Integer underflow (CWE-191): Unsigned subtraction that wraps to a large value, especially in length computations.

- Race condition (CWE-362/367): Shared state modified without proper synchronization, or TOCTOU between check and use.

  - Race conditions in code that is architecturally single-threaded or where the lock scope matches the access scope

Based on surviving evidence from Phase 4:

If one or more findings survived ALL verification steps:
- vulnerable = true
- Report the CWE(s) only for verified finding(s), using the most specific CWE from Step D
- Cite the exact code location (line numbers and code snippet) for each finding
- Confidence reflects evidence strength: use 0.9+ only when you have a fully concrete trigger

If NO findings survived verification:

- Confidence reflects analysis thoroughness

static int sctp_setsockopt_auth_key(struct sock *sk,
				    char __user *optval,
				    int optlen)
{
	struct sctp_authkey *authkey;
	struct sctp_association *asoc;
	int ret;

	if (!sctp_auth_enable)
		return -EACCES;

	if (optlen <= sizeof(struct sctp_authkey))
		return -EINVAL;

	authkey = kmalloc(optlen, GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!authkey)
		return -ENOMEM;

	if (copy_from_user(authkey, optval, optlen)) {
		ret = -EFAULT;
		goto out;
	}

	if (authkey->sca_keylength > optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)) {
		ret = -EINVAL;
		goto out;
	}

	asoc = sctp_id2assoc(sk, authkey->sca_assoc_id);
	if (!asoc && authkey->sca_assoc_id && sctp_style(sk, UDP)) {
		ret = -EINVAL;
		goto out;
	}

	ret = sctp_auth_set_key(sctp_sk(sk)->ep, asoc, authkey);
out:
	kfree(authkey);
	return ret;
}

static int smtp_command_parse_parameters(struct smtp_command_parser *parser)
{
	const unsigned char *p, *mp;
	uoff_t max_size = (parser->auth_response ?
		parser->limits.max_auth_size :
		parser->limits.max_parameters_size);
	int nch = 1;

	/* We assume parameters to match textstr (HT, SP, Printable US-ASCII).
	   For command parameters, we also accept valid UTF-8 characters.
	 */
	p = parser->cur + parser->state.poff;
	while (p < parser->end) {
		unichar_t ch;

		if (parser->auth_response)
			ch = *p;
		else {
			nch = uni_utf8_get_char_n(p, (size_t)(p - parser->end),
						  &ch);
		}
		if (nch == 0)
			break;
		if (nch < 0) {
			smtp_command_parser_error(parser,
				SMTP_COMMAND_PARSE_ERROR_BAD_COMMAND,
				"Invalid UTF-8 character in command parameters");
			return -1;
		}
		if ((parser->auth_response || (ch & 0x80) == 0x00) &&
		    !smtp_char_is_textstr((unsigned char)ch))
			break;
		p += nch;
	}
	if (max_size > 0 && (uoff_t)(p - parser->cur) > max_size) {
		smtp_command_parser_error(parser,
			SMTP_COMMAND_PARSE_ERROR_LINE_TOO_LONG,
			"%s line is too long",
			(parser->auth_response ?
				"AUTH response" : "Command"));
		return -1;
	}
	parser->state.poff = p - parser->cur;
	if (p == parser->end || nch == 0)
		return 0;

	/* In the interest of improved interoperability, SMTP receivers SHOULD
	   tolerate trailing white space before the terminating <CRLF>.

	   WSP =  SP / HTAB ; white space

	   --> Trim the end of the buffer
	 */
	mp = p;
	if (mp > parser->cur) {
		while (mp > parser->cur && (*(mp-1) == ' ' || *(mp-1) == '\t'))
			mp--;
	}

	if (!parser->auth_response && mp > parser->cur && *parser->cur == ' ') {
		smtp_command_parser_error(parser,
			SMTP_COMMAND_PARSE_ERROR_BAD_COMMAND,
			"Duplicate space after command name");
		return -1;
	}

	parser->state.cmd_params = i_strdup_until(parser->cur, mp);
	parser->cur = p;
	parser->state.poff = 0;
	return 1;
}

{
    auto* zei = entries.getUnchecked (index);
